pages.text: Life too small to see: bacteria, the viruses that eat them, and the fungi that feel their way through the ground.

$(thing)Microbiology$(): the $(item)Fermenter$() grows $(item)Bacterial Cultures$() with air. $(thing)Biomineralisation$(): magnetotactic bacteria, kept short of air (1 to 10%), grow $(item)Magnetite$() from iron nuggets. $(thing)Probiotics$(): lactobacilli, with no air at all, make the $(item)Probiotic Seal$(), an upgrade that keeps a Biology console from ever being contaminated.

$(thing)Viruses$(): the $(item)Phage Lab$() sets how many phages each cell meets. The share hit is 1 − e^(−MOI), and each bursts after its latent period; too many phages burst the cells from outside. $(thing)Lysogeny$(): phages that write themselves into a genome deliver genes, a cheap Recombinant DNA.

$(thing)Mycology$(): the $(item)Mycelium Bed$() grows mould from old bread: growth peaks at its temperature and wants damp, but too wet and bacteria take the bed. Mould gives $(item)Antibiotics$(): cheap cleaning for a contaminated machine, but each dose on the same machine works less often. That is resistance, made by selection.
$(thing)Slime Moulds$(): $(item)Physarum$() links food sources with the shortest network it can, and makes Network Maps cheaply: Mathematics' graphs, alive.
